item.title: Cedric
item.description:
Cedric acts as a stand-in for meetings. A user gives it slides, notes, and background documents, and it attends a call, presents, and responds to questions using that material. When it does not know something, it can note the question for follow-up.

The idea appeals to people with a heavy meeting load, such as founders or sales teams running repeated demos. It raises etiquette and trust questions: others in the meeting should know they are talking to an AI agent.

item.title: ClawsGO Science
item.description:
ClawsGO Science goes beyond literature review. The agent can plan an analysis, write and run code in a cloud environment, process datasets, and report results with the steps shown. It is built for scientific work such as data analysis and computational experiments.

Doing the work, not only describing it, can speed up exploratory research. Results still need scrutiny, since an agent can make statistical or coding mistakes, and reproducibility depends on seeing exactly what was run.

item.title: Testifly
item.description:
Testifly uses AI agents to test web applications. A team gives it a URL and login details, and the system explores the app, plans test cases, generates tests, and runs them, then heals tests when the UI changes. The aim is coverage without writing and maintaining scripts.

Autonomous testing can find regressions that no one thought to cover, and reduces the upkeep that makes automated tests brittle. Results still need review, since passing tests do not prove the right behavior is checked.

item.title: UnleashX
item.description:
UnleashX provides voice and workflow automation. Teams configure AI agents that handle phone conversations and carry out actions across systems, such as calling leads, qualifying them, updating records, and sending follow-ups. Rules define what the worker may do.

The platform presents these as digital employees for roles like sales development and support. Outbound calling needs consent and compliance with telemarketing rules, and AI voice agents should disclose themselves.

UnleashX is paid, and independent information is limited, so run a pilot first. Alternatives include Bland AI, Retell AI, Vapi, Synthflow, and 11x. UnleashX suits small teams automating calls and follow-ups.

item.title: DeepSeek Super-Agent
item.description:
Super-Agent explores what a team-facing coding agent could look like. Built on DeepSeek’s Harness runtime, it is tied to one GitHub repository and listens for requests from approved colleagues in Feishu, a workplace chat app. A teammate can ask it to investigate or change something, and it works on the code and reports back.

The prototype shows how a lab thinks about agents inside everyday collaboration tools instead of only in a developer’s terminal. Because it is a prototype, it focuses on demonstrating the design, not on a polished product with broad integrations, and it requires technical setup.
